question: Mahatma Gandhi abruptly called off the Non-Cooperation Movement when in ________ a crowd of peasants set fire to a police station in Chauri Chaura.
solution:
The correct answer is __**February 1922.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Non-Cooperation Movement was a major political protest in India that began in 1920 and lasted for two years.**
 
• The movement was led by **Mahatma Gandhi and was aimed at achieving independence from British rule.**
 
• The movement was successful in mobilizing a large number of people and in bringing about a number of changes, such as the repeal of the **Rowlatt Act.**
 
• However, the movement was also marked by violence, and in** February 1922, a crowd of peasants set fire to a police station in Chauri Chaura, killing 22 policemen.**
 
• This incident led to Gandhi calling off the movement, as he believed that it had become violent and that it was no longer in the best interests of India.
 
• The **Chauri Chaura incident was a major setback for the Indian independence movement, but it also served as a reminder of the importance of non-violence.**
 
• **Gandhi's decision to call off the movement was a difficult one, but it was a decision that he believed was in the best interests of India.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• About Mahatma Gandhi:

 
 
• Mahatma Gandhi (Mohandas Karamchand Gandhi) was born on October 2, 1869.
 
• He died January 30, 1948, in Delhi, and the day is celebrated as Shaheed Diwas or Martyrs' Day.
 
 
 
• His autobiography is titled My Experiments with Truth.
 
• Other Important movements led by Mahatma Gandhi:
 
 
• ​Champaran Movement (1917)
 
• Kheda Movement (1918)
 
• Khilafat Movement (1919)
 
• Civil Disobedience Movement: Dandi March (1930)
 
• Quit India Movement (1942)
